sourceNotes: Seeded from SEM roleplay performance indicators and marketing cluster exam data.
Terms are scoped for future vocab-card, quiz, and event-filter UI use.

terms.definition: The path a product takes from producer or provider to the final customer.
terms.whyItMatters: Channel choices affect convenience, cost, access, and customer experience.

terms.definition: Giving full attention, checking understanding, and responding thoughtfully to a speaker.
terms.whyItMatters: Judges expect competitors to handle questions and concerns clearly.

terms.definition: Tangible products in limited supply that must be produced and purchased.
terms.whyItMatters: Distinguishing goods from services underlies every business model.

terms.definition: The sales level where total revenue equals total costs.
terms.whyItMatters: Break-even shows the minimum sales a price or product strategy needs to be viable.

terms.definition: The overall approach a business uses to reach customers and meet marketing goals.
terms.whyItMatters: Case studies require strategies that fit business objectives and market conditions.

terms.definition: The activities a business uses to build satisfaction, trust, and loyalty.
terms.whyItMatters: Strong customer relations support repeat business and reputation.

terms.definition: Helping customers make purchase decisions through planned communication.
terms.whyItMatters: Selling vocabulary supports recommendations about staff, service, and revenue.

terms.definition: Planning, developing, marketing, and managing offerings across their life.
terms.whyItMatters: It ensures offerings meet customer needs and generate sustainable revenue.

terms.definition: Facts and figures that have been processed into a meaningful, usable form for decisions.
terms.whyItMatters: Competitors must know that raw data becomes useful only once it is organized and interpreted.

terms.definition: Communication that informs, persuades, and reminds customers about offerings.
terms.whyItMatters: Promotion choices must fit the audience, message, and budget.

terms.definition: The ability to understand and manage emotions in yourself and others.
terms.whyItMatters: It underlies teamwork, service, and conflict-resolution answers.

terms.definition: A distribution path where a producer sells straight to customers with no intermediaries.
terms.whyItMatters: Direct channels maximize control and margin but demand more sales and logistics effort.

terms.definition: Signals such as facial expressions, gestures, and posture that carry meaning without words.
terms.whyItMatters: Reading cues lets competitors adjust to a customer's or judge's reaction.

terms.definition: The inputs — land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship — used to produce goods and services.
terms.whyItMatters: Managing limited resources is central to operations and strategy.

terms.definition: The amount or percentage added to a product's cost to set its selling price.
terms.whyItMatters: Markup links cost directly to a pricing recommendation.

terms.definition: Discovering and defining the markets where a business can sell its offering.
terms.whyItMatters: Identifying the right market is the foundation of any marketing plan.

terms.definition: The assistance and support a business provides to meet customer needs.
terms.whyItMatters: Service quality is central to satisfaction and retention.

terms.definition: The structured steps that move a customer from awareness to purchase.
terms.whyItMatters: Knowing the process helps competitors execute each stage well.

terms.definition: The stages a product passes through: introduction, growth, maturity, and decline.
terms.whyItMatters: The stage a product is in drives its marketing, pricing, and distribution.

terms.definition: Raw, unprocessed facts and figures collected through observation, measurement, or research.
terms.whyItMatters: All information management begins with knowing what counts as reliable data.

terms.definition: The blend of advertising, publicity, sales promotion, and personal selling.
terms.whyItMatters: A mix lets competitors recommend more than one communication path.

terms.definition: A realistic sense of your own value and capabilities.
terms.whyItMatters: Strong self-esteem improves decision-making and leadership effectiveness.

terms.definition: A distribution path where one or more intermediaries sit between producer and customer.
terms.whyItMatters: Indirect channels widen reach and share costs but reduce producer control.

terms.definition: A structured conversation among several people to share ideas and reach conclusions.
terms.whyItMatters: Team events depend on effective group discussion.

terms.definition: The relationship between how much of a good is available and how much customers want to buy.
terms.whyItMatters: It explains pricing, scarcity, inventory, and opportunity.

terms.definition: The percentage of revenue left as profit after costs are subtracted.
terms.whyItMatters: Margin reflects pricing effectiveness against financial goals.

terms.definition: The specific customer group a business chooses as its primary marketing audience.
terms.whyItMatters: Recommendations are stronger when they name a specific audience.

terms.definition: A relationship of mutual understanding and trust between a business and its customers.
terms.whyItMatters: Building rapport raises trust and the odds of repeat business.

terms.definition: Identifying and qualifying potential customers who may need an offering.
terms.whyItMatters: Effective prospecting builds the foundation for successful sales.

terms.definition: The full range of products and services a company offers.
terms.whyItMatters: Product-mix decisions shape positioning, resources, and revenue.

terms.definition: An organized, computer-managed collection of related data that can be stored and retrieved systematically.
terms.whyItMatters: Businesses run everything from inventory to customer records on databases.

terms.definition: Paid, nonpersonal communication delivered through media to large audiences.
terms.whyItMatters: Advertising builds broad brand awareness efficiently and at scale.

terms.definition: Belief in your ability to perform well and reach your goals.
terms.whyItMatters: Confidence persuades others and drives initiative in competitive settings.

terms.definition: A business between producer and customer, such as a retailer, wholesaler, or agent.
terms.whyItMatters: Intermediaries expand reach but add cost and control tradeoffs.

terms.definition: A formal written message with a clear subject, correct grammar, and appropriate tone.
terms.whyItMatters: Written events reward mastery of email conventions.

terms.definition: The rivalry among businesses to attract the same customers.
terms.whyItMatters: Competitive pressure shapes pricing, service, product mix, and promotion.

terms.definition: A plan for setting prices to meet business objectives and positioning.
terms.whyItMatters: A sound strategy is central to case presentations and positioning.

terms.definition: A written document laying out marketing objectives, strategies, and tactics for a period.
terms.whyItMatters: The plan guides all promotional and customer-facing decisions.

terms.definition: A mindset committed to meeting customer needs and providing quality help.
terms.whyItMatters: It helps employees deliver consistent, customer-focused interactions.

terms.definition: The opening contact and strategy used to engage a potential customer.
terms.whyItMatters: A professional approach sets the first impression that drives interest.

terms.definition: A group of related products sold under one brand or category.
terms.whyItMatters: Line decisions balance customer choice against cost and complexity.

terms.definition: A software application that organizes data in rows and columns for calculation and analysis.
terms.whyItMatters: Spreadsheets are a core business tool competitors are expected to use comfortably.

terms.definition: Short-term incentives like coupons, contests, and discounts that spur purchases.
terms.whyItMatters: Promotions drive quick sales, trial, and inventory clearance.

terms.definition: Taking independent action to solve problems or seize opportunities.
terms.whyItMatters: Initiative marks leaders who drive results without waiting for direction.

terms.definition: An intermediary that buys goods in bulk from producers and resells them to retailers.
terms.whyItMatters: Wholesalers aggregate inventory and provide the logistics that enable retail networks.

terms.definition: A formal document in standard format used for official outside communication.
terms.whyItMatters: Judges expect correct formatting, tone, and structure.

terms.definition: The money left after a business subtracts all costs and expenses from revenue.
terms.whyItMatters: The profit motive drives the decisions competitors must justify.

terms.definition: Setting price by adding a standard markup to a product's cost.
terms.whyItMatters: It is a foundational method when a price must ensure cost recovery.

terms.definition: An assessment of internal and external factors affecting a business's marketing.
terms.whyItMatters: Understanding the situation must come before any recommendation.

terms.definition: The commitment a company makes about the value and experience it will deliver.
terms.whyItMatters: Knowing the promise helps employees deliver a consistent experience.
